newsitem.title: USA: Transatlantic crudes still scarce on US Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: Transatlantic crudes still scarce on US Gulf Coast.

text.p: Transatlantic barrels remained scarce on the U.S. Gulf Coast Thursday, boosting refiner interest in domestic grades and short-haul Latin American barrels, traders said.
The spread between bellwethers West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent for March was at $1.50-60 a barrel Thursday afternoon, rendering transatlantic trade uneconomic.
A hodgepodge of West African cargoes is still on offer, however, despite thin demand on the U.S. Gulf Coast, where several refiners are in turnarounds.

In Latin America, Bolivia's state-owned oil company Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB) is close to awarding a tender for 250,000 barrels of 45-API gravity reconstituted crude oil for loading February 24.
Four companies are vying for the award.
Meanwhile, the market appears to have shaken off its initial jitters from an ongoing public-sector strike in Colombia.
The strike, now in its third day, has not affected crude loadings and U.S. refiners awaiting spot cargoes in March have expressed confidence that their contracts will be met.
Two major European equity producers in Colombian said market availablities could actually increase because some local refineries aren't running at full capacity and domestic demand is down.
